title: Designed protein binders that enter cells and engage intracellular targets

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 9, Cell-penetrating protein binders. Target: zero-shot designed protein binders that engage preregistered intracellular targets in living cells when applied extracellularly, without transfection, electroporation or similar methods; the full challenge is 20 targets at an 80% success rate. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Zero-shot design of cell-penetrating protein binders
page.definition: Designed protein binders enter living cells after extracellular administration and bind intracellular targets. Zero-shot means no target-specific experimental screening, evolution or optimization before evaluation.

goal.need: A CFTR-binding nanobody illustrates the delivery problem: its cell-free affinity was nanomolar, while functional rescue used micromolar extracellular dosing. CFTR is a chloride channel whose intracellular nucleotide-binding domain is bound by the nanobody. The study identifies crowding, intracellular distribution and target accessibility as possible contributors to this concentration gap.

figures.caption: Cell-free binding and cellular rescue conditions reported on 17 April 2026.
figures.note: Affinity and treatment concentrations measure different properties. CFTR inhibitor-sensitive current measurements included 18 treated and 18 vehicle-control monolayer inserts; the affinity value was cited from earlier work.

statements.quote: Demonstrate the ability to produce protein binders against intracellular targets.
statements.context: The stated goal of Millennium Problem 09.

statements.quote: overcome the challenges associated with broad, intracellular delivery of biologics to diverse cell and tissue types
statements.context: Hermes addresses intracellular delivery broadly; it does not require zero-shot binder design.

completion.title: Zero-shot binders engage 16 of 20 preregistered intracellular targets under Problem 09’s conditions.
completion.criterion: Engage at least 16 of 20 preregistered intracellular protein targets in living cells after extracellular dosing at pharmacologically supported concentrations. Produce designs within 24 hours after preregistration, without further evolution or optimization; permit no wet-lab work before evaluation except assay-protein production. Cell entry must be therapeutically plausible; transfection, intrabody expression, electroporation, membrane disruption and similar methods are excluded.
completion.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, Millennium Problems for Biology, Problem 09.
completion.threshold_quote: 20 preregistered targets with an 80% success rate.
completion.basis: This challenge explicitly combines prospective binder design, extracellular administration and intracellular engagement. Its numerical engagement and concentration acceptance cutoffs remain unspecified.

milestones.title: A designed protein binds an intracellular target in a purified-protein binding assay.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate experimental binding to an intracellular protein using the binding-validation convention applied in BindCraft and AlphaProteo. These studies do not establish a shared affinity cutoff. On 27 August 2025, BindCraft reported binding for all 6 tested SpCas9 binders; two had estimated surface plasmon resonance affinities around 300 nM, with incomplete titration curves.
milestones.set_by: Experimental protein-design convention, exemplified by Pacesa et al., Figure 1b, and Zambaldi et al., experimental validation.
milestones.threshold_quote: where binding was observed on SPR measurement

milestones.title: An extracellularly applied protein binder reaches the cytosol in an expected-size protein form.
milestones.criterion: Detect a binder-sized protein band in a cytosolic fraction excluding endosomes and nuclei. Franz et al. detected fluorescent NB1 after extracellular dosing and 24 hours after nanobody removal. Quantitative fractionation used 1 distinct sample per condition. This establishes access to the cytosol, the cellular fluid outside membrane-bound organelles.
milestones.set_by: Compartment-specific delivery-validation convention used by Franz et al., Extended Data Figure 2, and Shin et al., Figure 2.
milestones.threshold_quote: These observations confirm successful cytosolic delivery

milestones.title: An extracellularly applied protein binder physically associates with an intracellular target.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate intracellular target association with cellular localization evidence and biochemical recovery of the binder–target complex. On 10 May 2017, Shin et al. reported RT11 association with KRasG12V in SW480 cells after extracellular treatment at 2 µM for 12 hours, supported by microscopy and immunoprecipitation from endosome-depleted lysates. Images represented at least 2 independent experiments. RT11 required screening and affinity maturation.
milestones.set_by: Intracellular target-engagement convention applied by Shin et al., Figure 2b–c; their published example concerns RAS.
milestones.threshold_quote: revealed the physical interaction of RT11 with cytosolic KRas mutants after internalization

milestones.title: A binder engages a preregistered intracellular target under Problem 09’s zero-shot conditions.
milestones.criterion: Satisfy Problem 09’s design-time, dosing, delivery and engagement requirements for an individual preregistered intracellular protein target before demonstrating panel-wide success.
milestones.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, Problem 09’s per-target requirements; the document does not designate this as a separate intermediate award.

not_found: Problem 09 specifies no numerical target-engagement cutoff, supported concentration range, required cell type, replicate count or target-selection procedure.
Searches of Problem 09, binder-design benchmarks and intracellular-delivery programmes found no separately published intermediate target-count threshold.
No public preregistered result satisfying Problem 09’s combined per-target conditions or its 20-target completion test was found as of 14 November 2026.

results.finding: All 6 of 6 designed SpCas9 binders bound the purified intracellular target.
results.detail: The two top binders showed apparent SPR affinities around 300 nM, although complete titration curves were difficult to obtain.

results.finding: CFBE41o- cells: NB1 was detected in the cytosolic fraction 24 hours after removal; n=1 sample per condition.
results.detail: Fluorescent NB1 bands were measured after fractionation excluding endosomes and nuclei. Whole-cell lysates showed a band at the expected molecular weight.
results.quote: Twenty-five hours after initial nanobody application, the amount of nanobody detected in the cytosolic fraction and the total cellular content appear equilibrated, albeit lower relative to the amounts observed at 1 hour after nanobody application

results.finding: RT11 associated with intracellular KRasG12V in SW480 cells; images represented at least 2 independent experiments.
results.detail: After extracellular treatment with 2 µM RT11 for 12 hours, microscopy showed colocalization and immunoprecipitation recovered the complex from endosome-depleted lysates. RT11 required target-specific screening and affinity maturation.
